This design is extremely rare in remote sensing pretraining research—most papers change architecture, dataset, and algorithm simultaneously, making results impossible to attribute. v1.1's approach makes the performance difference between the two versions point precisely to the effect of the token merging strategy. f5x1c1:256: OlmoEarth v1.1's efficiency breakthrough comes not from architectural restructuring but from fine-tuning the data encoding strategy—merging Sentinel-2's 3 resolution tokens into 1, directly cutting token count by 2/3. But this operation has an engineering cost: naive merging causes a 10-percentage-point performance regression, showing that modeling spatial relationships between bands is critical for remote sensing tasks. The team compensated for this loss by modifying the pretraining strategy, ultimately achieving the dual goal of "3x efficiency + comparable performance." This case shows that on large Transformer models, fine-grained data encoding design is often a higher-leverage optimization than architectural innovation.
